mods.title: Minecraft Mods. Free Mod Browser & One-Click Installer | GDLauncher
mods.description: Browse and install thousands of Minecraft mods from CurseForge and Modrinth. Forge, Fabric, NeoForge, and Quilt support. One-click install with automatic dependency resolution.
mods.intro: Mods add new content, features, and improvements to Minecraft. Install them easily with GDLauncher's built-in mod browser.
mods.section.what.heading: What are Mods?
mods.section.what.p1: Mods (short for modifications) are community-created additions that change or enhance Minecraft. They can add new blocks, items, mobs, dimensions, game mechanics, and much more.
mods.section.what.li.content: Content. New items, blocks, dimensions, and mobs
mods.section.what.li.tech: Tech. Machines, automation, and power systems
mods.section.what.li.magic: Magic. Spells, rituals, and magical systems
mods.section.what.li.qol: Quality of Life. UI improvements and convenience features
mods.section.what.li.performance: Performance. FPS optimization and faster loading
mods.section.loaders.heading: Mod Loaders Explained
mods.section.loaders.intro: Mods require a mod loader to run. The main options are:
mods.section.loaders.forge: Forge. The original mod loader (2011). Largest mod library with complex mods like Tinkers' Construct, Create, and Twilight Forest. Slower to update for new Minecraft versions.
mods.section.loaders.fabric: Fabric. Lightweight and fast-updating. Popular for performance mods and newer Minecraft versions. Large mod library on Modrinth.
mods.section.loaders.neoforge: NeoForge. A 2023 fork of Forge by the original development team. Modern improvements with better performance. Increasingly the standard for Forge-style mods on 1.20.4+.
mods.section.loaders.quilt: Quilt. A Fabric fork focused on community governance. Compatible with most Fabric mods plus its own additions.
mods.section.loaders.outro: Most mods are made for either Forge/NeoForge OR Fabric, not both. Always check which loader a mod requires before installing.
mods.section.compat.heading: Mod Compatibility
mods.section.compat.intro: Key things to know about mod compatibility:
mods.section.compat.li.version: Mods must match your Minecraft version exactly (a 1.20.1 mod won't work on 1.20.4)
mods.section.compat.li.server: All players on a server usually need the same mods installed
mods.section.compat.li.client: Some mods are "client-side only" (like minimaps) and don't need server installation
mods.section.compat.li.conflict: Mods can conflict with each other, check mod pages for known incompatibilities
mods.section.compat.li.major: Major Minecraft updates (like 1.13, 1.17, 1.20) often break mods until authors update them

modpacks.section.what.heading: What is a Modpack?
modpacks.section.what.p1: A modpack is a pre-configured collection of Minecraft mods designed to work together. Instead of manually installing dozens of individual mods, modpacks give you everything you need for a specific gameplay experience in one download.
modpacks.section.what.li.kitchen: Kitchen Sink. Hundreds of mods with everything you could want
modpacks.section.what.li.tech: Tech. Focus on machines, automation, and engineering
modpacks.section.what.li.magic: Magic. Spells, rituals, and mystical adventures
modpacks.section.what.li.lightweight: Lightweight. Enhanced vanilla with quality of life improvements
modpacks.section.complexity.heading: Modpack Complexity Levels
modpacks.section.complexity.intro: Modpacks vary in complexity and hardware requirements:
modpacks.section.complexity.li.lightweig: Lightweight (50–100 mods), 4 GB RAM, any modern PC. Examples: Fabulously Optimized, Simply Optimized
modpacks.section.complexity.li.medium: Medium (100–200 mods), 6–8 GB RAM, mid-range hardware. Examples: All The Mods, Better Minecraft
modpacks.section.complexity.li.heavy: Heavy (200–400+ mods), 8–12 GB RAM, powerful hardware. Examples: All The Mods 9, Vault Hunters, Create: Above and Beyond
modpacks.section.complexity.outro: GDLauncher automatically allocates the recommended RAM for each modpack based on its requirements.
modpacks.section.choose.heading: Finding the Right Modpack
modpacks.section.choose.intro: Consider these factors when choosing a modpack:
modpacks.section.choose.li.progression: Progression style. Guided quests vs sandbox exploration
modpacks.section.choose.li.theme: Theme. Tech, magic, adventure, or kitchen sink (everything)
modpacks.section.choose.li.difficulty: Difficulty. Casual, expert, or hardcore modes
modpacks.section.choose.li.multiplayer: Multiplayer. Some modpacks are designed specifically for servers
modpacks.section.choose.li.updates: Updates. Active modpacks receive bug fixes; abandoned ones don't
modpacks.section.choose.outro: CurseForge hosts the largest collection of modpacks, while Modrinth offers a curated selection with faster downloads.

modpacks.browse.intro: Find and install modpacks from CurseForge and Modrinth with one click. We handle Java, memory, and updates automatically.
modpacks.browse.li.oneclick: One-click install with auto Java setup
shaders.section.what.heading: What are Shaders?
shaders.section.what.p1: Shaders are graphical modifications that completely overhaul how Minecraft looks. They add effects that aren't possible in vanilla Minecraft, creating stunning visuals.
shaders.section.what.li.shadows: Dynamic Shadows. Realistic shadows that move with the sun
shaders.section.what.li.water: Water Reflections. Reflective, transparent water with waves
shaders.section.what.li.volumetric: Volumetric Lighting. God rays streaming through trees
shaders.section.what.li.atmosphere: Atmospheric Effects. Fog, clouds, and weather improvements
shaders.section.what.li.colors: Improved Colors. Better saturation and color grading
shaders.section.loaders.heading: Shader Loaders
shaders.section.loaders.intro: Shaders require a shader loader to work. The two main options are:
shaders.section.loaders.iris: Iris + Sodium (Fabric/Quilt). Open-source with significantly better performance. Often delivers 2× the FPS of OptiFine. Updates quickly for new Minecraft versions and works with most OptiFine shader packs.
shaders.section.loaders.optifine: OptiFine (Forge or standalone). The original shader loader since 2011. Also includes connected textures, zoom, and other visual features. Closed-source with slower updates for new versions.
shaders.section.loaders.outro: For best performance, we recommend Iris + Sodium. GDLauncher installs Iris and Sodium one-click from the Addons browser; OptiFine has to be added manually to a Forge instance.
shaders.section.perf.heading: Performance Considerations
shaders.section.perf.intro: Shaders are GPU-intensive. Here's what to expect based on shader complexity:
shaders.section.perf.li.light: Lightweight shaders (Sildur's Lite, Complementary Reimagined). Playable on integrated graphics
shaders.section.perf.li.medium: Medium shaders (BSL, Complementary). Need a dedicated GPU (GTX 1060 / RX 580 or better)
shaders.section.perf.li.heavy: Heavy shaders (SEUS PTGI, Continuum RT). Need a powerful GPU (RTX 3060 or better)
shaders.section.perf.tip.render: Lower render distance (8–12 chunks with shaders)
shaders.section.perf.tip.disable: Disable shader features you don't need (reflections, volumetric lighting)
shaders.section.perf.tip.sodium: Use performance mods like Sodium alongside Iris
shaders.browse.heading: Browse Shaders in GDLauncher
shaders.browse.intro: Find and install stunning shader packs from CurseForge and Modrinth directly in GDLauncher. We'll help you set up Iris or OptiFine automatically.
resourcepacks.section.what.heading: What are Resource Packs?
resourcepacks.section.what.p1: Resource packs (formerly texture packs) replace Minecraft's default visuals and audio. They can completely change the game's style without adding any new content.
resourcepacks.section.what.li.hd: HD Textures. Higher resolution block and item textures
resourcepacks.section.what.li.styled: Stylized Looks. Cartoon, realistic, or themed appearances
resourcepacks.section.what.li.connected: Connected Textures. Seamless glass, bookshelves, and more
resourcepacks.section.what.li.sounds: Custom Sounds. New music, ambient sounds, and effects
resourcepacks.section.what.li.models: 3D Models. Items and blocks with custom 3D shapes
resourcepacks.section.resolution.heading: Resolution Tiers
resourcepacks.section.resolution.intro: Resource packs come in different resolutions, measured in pixels per block face:
resourcepacks.section.resolution.li.16: 16× (Vanilla default). Runs on any hardware, classic pixel art style
resourcepacks.section.resolution.li.64: 64×. Noticeable detail increase, needs decent hardware
resourcepacks.section.resolution.li.128: 128×. High detail, needs a good GPU
resourcepacks.section.resolution.li.256: 256×–512×. Extreme detail, needs powerful hardware and OptiFine or the Continuity mod
resourcepacks.section.resolution.outro: Higher resolutions use more VRAM. A 256× pack might use 2–4 GB of VRAM compared to ~500 MB for vanilla textures.
resourcepacks.section.advanced.heading: Advanced Features
resourcepacks.section.advanced.intro: Modern resource packs can include advanced features that may require additional mods:
resourcepacks.section.advanced.li.connec: Connected Textures. Glass and bookshelves blend seamlessly (requires OptiFine or Continuity mod)
resourcepacks.section.advanced.li.cit: Custom Item Textures (CIT). Renamed items get unique textures (requires OptiFine or CIT Resewn mod)
resourcepacks.section.advanced.li.animat: Animated Textures. Flowing lava, waving plants, glowing effects
resourcepacks.section.advanced.li.cem: Custom Entity Models (CEM). Reshaped mobs and items (requires OptiFine or Entity Model Features mod)
resourcepacks.section.advanced.li.pbr: PBR/POM Textures. Realistic lighting and depth effects (requires shader support)
resourcepacks.section.advanced.outro: Check the resource pack description to see if it requires any mods for full functionality.

resourcepacks.browse.intro: Find and install resource packs from CurseForge and Modrinth directly in GDLauncher. Transform your game's look with just a few clicks.

datapacks.section.what.heading: What are Data Packs?
datapacks.section.what.p1: Data packs are a vanilla Minecraft feature that lets you customize game behavior. They're perfect for adding tweaks without needing a mod loader.
datapacks.section.what.li.recipes: Crafting Recipes. Add or change how items are crafted
datapacks.section.what.li.loot: Loot Tables. Modify what mobs drop and chest contents
datapacks.section.what.li.advancements: Advancements. Add custom achievements and rewards
datapacks.section.what.li.worldgen: World Generation. Change biome distribution and structures
datapacks.section.vsmods.heading: Data Packs vs Mods
datapacks.section.vsmods.intro: Data packs and mods serve different purposes:
datapacks.section.vsmods.dp.li.drop: Drop directly into your world folder, no mod loader needed
datapacks.section.vsmods.dp.li.vanilla: Limited to vanilla mechanics (can't add new blocks or mobs)
datapacks.section.vsmods.dp.li.server: Only needed on the server, clients stay vanilla
datapacks.section.vsmods.dp.li.survive: Usually survive Minecraft updates without breaking
datapacks.section.vsmods.mods.li.loader: Require a mod loader (Forge, Fabric, etc.)
datapacks.section.vsmods.mods.li.content: Can add entirely new content, mechanics, and systems
datapacks.section.vsmods.mods.li.both: Usually needed on both server and client
datapacks.section.vsmods.mods.li.break: Often break when Minecraft updates until the author patches them
datapacks.section.vsmods.outro: Data packs are perfect for vanilla-compatible tweaks. Use mods when you need entirely new content or mechanics.
datapacks.section.capabilities.heading: Full Capabilities
datapacks.section.capabilities.intro: Data packs can modify many vanilla systems. Introduced in Minecraft 1.13 (2018), they're officially supported by Mojang:
datapacks.section.capabilities.li.recipe: Recipes. Add new crafting recipes or modify existing ones
datapacks.section.capabilities.li.loot: Loot tables. Change mob drops, chest contents, fishing loot
datapacks.section.capabilities.li.advanc: Advancements. Create custom achievements with rewards
datapacks.section.capabilities.li.worldg: World generation. Modify biome placement, structures, ore distribution
datapacks.section.capabilities.li.functi: Functions. Run command sequences (like command blocks, but file-based)
datapacks.section.capabilities.li.predic: Predicates. Create complex conditions for game events
datapacks.section.capabilities.li.tags: Tags. Group blocks/items for consistent behavior

datapacks.browse.intro: Find and install data packs from CurseForge and Modrinth directly in GDLauncher. Enhance vanilla Minecraft without needing mods.

worlds.section.what.heading: What are World Downloads?
worlds.section.what.p1: World downloads are save files created by other players that you can play on your own computer. They contain everything from the original world, builds, items, and configurations.
worlds.section.what.li.adventure: Adventure Maps. Story-driven experiences with puzzles and quests
worlds.section.what.li.minigame: Minigame Maps. Parkour, PvP arenas, escape rooms
worlds.section.what.li.survival: Survival Maps. Pre-built worlds with unique challenges
worlds.section.what.li.creative: Creative Showcases. Amazing builds to explore
worlds.section.what.li.redstone: Redstone Contraptions. Working machines and mechanisms
worlds.section.compat.heading: Compatibility Notes
worlds.section.compat.intro: World downloads work with any Minecraft edition, but keep these things in mind:
worlds.section.compat.li.match: The world's Minecraft version should match your game version for best results
worlds.section.compat.li.newer: Worlds made in newer versions won't open in older versions of Minecraft
worlds.section.compat.li.upgrade: Worlds from older versions will auto-upgrade when opened (this is one-way)
worlds.section.compat.li.modded: Modded worlds require the same mods to work properly
worlds.section.compat.li.commands: Some maps use command blocks that may behave differently across versions
worlds.section.compat.outro: GDLauncher makes installation easy, just browse, click install, and the world is added to your instance.
worlds.section.share.heading: Sharing Your Own Worlds
worlds.section.share.intro: You can share your own worlds with other players:
worlds.section.share.li.folder: Worlds are stored in your instance's saves folder
worlds.section.share.li.zip: Zip the world folder to create a shareable file
worlds.section.share.li.upload: Upload to CurseForge or Planet Minecraft, or share directly with friends
worlds.section.share.tip.spawn: Set a clear spawn point before sharing
worlds.section.share.tip.versionInfo: Include version info and any required mods or data packs in the description
worlds.section.share.tip.test: Test the world from a fresh download before publishing
worlds.section.share.tip.respack: Consider adding a resource pack if your build relies on specific textures

docs.what.heading: What is GDLauncher?
docs.what.body: GDLauncher is a custom Minecraft launcher that provides additional functionalities over the official Minecraft launcher, enabling users, among other things, to install and manage multiple instances of the game, each with its own set of mods and resource packs. You can find the full list of features below.

docs.features.li.addons: Install addons from CurseForge, Modrinth and more!
